title: Cyrus and the Postcard
premise: Marine biologist Emrys Eriksen has spent five years in the small coastal town of Saltmere cataloging sea turtles and keeping his heart under strict containment after a devastating betrayal. When his sister demands he bring a plus-one to the family reunion, he hires Wren Calloway, a charming local postcard artist, to play his boyfriend for a weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, but Emrys's old wounds—and a town land-grab scheme Wren is secretly investigating—force both of them to choose between safety and each other. When Emrys discovers Wren has been using their relationship as cover for her investigation, he must decide whether love built on a lie can become true, ultimately exposing the corruption and risking his whole heart just as Wren's visa deadline forces her to leave Saltmere—or stay for him.
about_author: August Sandoval is the pen name of a former marine research assistant who traded tide charts for love stories set on the water's edge. Having spent years in small coastal communities, Sandoval writes romances about guarded people learning that belonging is worth the risk.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On Saltmere's beach at dawn, Emrys logs a nesting loggerhead, methodical and alone, narrating his philosophy that hearts are trainable muscles. A phone call from his sister Mara demanding a plus-one to the family reunion rattles his careful containment. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility made visible.

chapters.title: The Postcard Stand
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Buying a coffee, Emrys lingers at Wren Calloway's postcard stand, drawn to her painting of the very beach he monitors. She teases him for being a regular who never talks. When he blurts out an absurd proposition—pretend to be his girlfriend—she surprises him by naming a price. Emotional beat: reckless hope disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over pier-side chowder, Emrys and Wren negotiate the rules: no real names of exes, no touching beyond hand-holding, no falling in love. Wren is warm but oddly evasive about why she needs cash so urgently. Emotional beat: a contract both of them are already breaking in spirit.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren studies Emrys's family photos, coaching him through stories about his own life he's never told anyone. Her POV reveals she's photographing harbor documents between takes—something about the marina expansion permits. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in the margins of a performance.

chapters.title: The Eriksen Reunion
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The reunion at his parents' beach house: Mara's probing, his father's cold appraisal, the cousin who knows Emrys's ex. Wren is magnetic, improvising a story about how they met at the postcard stand that is almost entirely true. Emotional beat: being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. During dessert, Emrys's father privately offers Wren money to leave, assuming she's a gold-digger—and Wren refuses with a fierceness that guts Emrys. On the porch afterward, their hands brush; neither pulls away. Emotional beat: the fake collapses; something uncontracted begins.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wakes at Emrys's guest room and flees before breakfast, ashamed of how real it felt. On the dock she photographs a shipping ledger she shouldn't have access to—evidence the marina project is a laundering front. Emotional beat: her secret investigation tightening around her like a net.

chapters.title: Second Date, Unplanned
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finds Wren sketching at the turtle sanctuary and, instead of ending the arrangement, asks her to dinner—no contract this time. She hesitates, then says yes. They walk the nesting beach at night and he tells her, haltingly, about the ex who stole his research and his trust. Emotional beat: first true confession.

chapters.title: The Nest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A hatchling emergence draws the whole town to the beach; Emrys and Wren guard the nest together through the night, shoulders touching. Wren realizes the marina project would destroy this very nesting ground. Emotional beat: love and stakes braiding together—the turtles, the town, the heart.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's contact in the harbor office warns her she's being watched. She considers telling Emrys everything but can't risk implicating him. Meanwhile she discovers her brother's debts—the reason she needs money—are tied to the same men. Emotional beat: the lie of omission becoming unbearable.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Weeks of real dates. Emrys offers Wren pieces of himself, carefully portioned, and she pushes back: 'You lend, you never give.' Their first fight. He storms off to the lab and finds his grant renewal contingent on supporting the marina project. Emotional beat: containment strategy failing on all fronts.

chapters.title: The Man from the Marina
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A slick developer named Corliss approaches Wren, offering to buy her silence—and her brother's debt forgiveness—if she hands over her photos. She stalls. That night Emrys sees her meeting Corliss and misreads it as intimacy. Emotional beat: jealousy and secrecy colliding at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Postmarked Betrayal
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts Wren; she deflects, and in anger he accuses her of being exactly what his father said. She walks out. Alone, he finds a postcard she painted of him at the nest—tender, unguarded—and realizes he got it wrong. Emotional beat: the low point; love misread as betrayal.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren decides to go to the state attorney alone, but Corliss's men break into her studio and steal her evidence, leaving a threat. She has one backup: a postcard mailed to herself with microfilm hidden under the stamp. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; justice outside the law begins.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Mara tells Emrys what their father did—offering Wren money—and Emrys finally understands the pattern: everyone he loves gets bought or leaves. He goes to Wren's studio, finds it ransacked, and waits through the night. Emotional beat: choosing to risk everything instead of lending pieces.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dawn at the sanctuary: Wren tells Emrys everything—the investigation, the debts, the stolen evidence, the postcard. Emrys, in turn, confesses he's been asked to endorse the marina and refuses. They become partners in truth. Emotional beat: the fake relationship finally, fully real.

chapters.title: The Public Record
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Emrys rebuild her case: Emrys's grant data proves the marina permits falsified turtle surveys. They plan to present everything at the town council hearing, knowing Corliss controls the council. Emotional beat: justice pursued outside the law, together, at real risk.

chapters.title: Corliss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Corliss offers Emrys a dream research position in exchange for burying the data—and reveals he knows about the postcard evidence and Wren's brother. Emrys records the threat on his phone. Emotional beat: power's corruption laid bare; Emrys refuses and becomes a target.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town council hearing: Corliss discredits Wren as a debt-ridden outsider, and the council moves to approve. Then Emrys takes the floor—play the recording, present the falsified surveys—and the town's fishermen, whom Wren quietly helped all along, stand with her. Emotional beat: the climax; the town itself becomes the jury.

chapters.title: After the Vote
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The council rejects the marina; Corliss is referred for investigation. But Wren is gone—her brother's debts settled by an anonymous payment, and a one-way bus ticket dated that morning. Emrys finds her studio empty except for one unfinished postcard: the two of them on the nesting beach. Emotional beat: victory hollowed by loss.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the bus out of Saltmere, Wren reads Emrys's voicemail: he isn't asking her to stay for him—he's offering her the sanctuary's artist-in-residence post, funded by the town, no strings. She realizes staying was never about him deciding for her; it's her choice to make. Emotional beat: the race against her own departure.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Postcard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren steps off the bus at the last stop before the highway and walks back to the nesting beach, where Emrys waits with the finished postcard she left behind—addressed to him, never mailed. They write the ending together and mail it to themselves, proof that they chose the whole heart. Epilogue beat: a year later, hatchlings, a gallery wall of postcards, home.
